phase.goal: PHASE 1 — INTELLIGENCE, BUSINESS FOUNDATION, TRUST ARCHITECTURE, AND PREMIUM EXPERIENCE

milestone.description: Repository/project foundation, durable multi-tenant state, provider abstraction

completed: P1-01: Repo/app foundation (Next.js 16 App Router, strict TypeScript, Tailwind 4, ESLint, Prettier, Vitest, Playwright, Prisma 7 + Postgres via Docker, env validation, deterministic health check)

P1-02: Data layer — User/Session/Organization/Membership/Project schema + migration, password hashing (scrypt), session lifecycle, tenant-aware authorization (requireOrganizationMembership/requireProjectAccess), organization/project service layer with tenant-isolation integration tests against a real Postgres test database

P1-03: Canonical Product State (append-only versioned), Product DNA (versioned with merge-not-erase partial updates), Product Memory (discrete typed entries), Product Knowledge relationships (typed node/edge graph with stable ids, same-project + no-self-loop constraints), all project-scoped and tenant-isolated

P1-04: AI provider abstraction (MockAIProvider fully implemented, AnthropicAIProvider stubbed for Phase 3), Intent Resolver, deterministic Impact Analysis foundation, product-facing Decision Ledger with disclosure tiers (ROUTINE/IMPORTANT/CONSEQUENTIAL) and approval flow, Orchestration Contract change-flow skeleton wiring them together

P1-05: Platform-wide versioned Supported Capability Registry mirroring Master Spec §4.3 classification exactly, seeded with truthful Phase 1 status (auth/tenancy SUPPORTED_NOW, generation/payments/mobile/AI/governance/distribution/billing correctly deferred with spec citations), and a Feasibility Engine that looks up capability keys against the registry rather than inventing feasibility claims
active: P1-06: Product Intelligence, Requirements Engine, Business Model Brief, unit economics

testStatus.unit: pass (19/19: env 4, slug 4, mock-provider 4, anthropic-provider 1, impact-analysis 6)
testStatus.integration: pass (62/62: users 5, session 5, tenancy 7, product-state 5, product-dna 6, product-memory 4, product-knowledge 5, decisions 7, intent-resolver 3, change-flow 2, capability-registry 5, seed-data 3, feasibility 5)

knownLimitations: Auth/tenancy/product-state/orchestration/registry exist only as a service/library layer — no UI, no Server Actions, no HTTP routes wire them up yet. That is P1-10/P1-11.
Tenant isolation is proven at the service+authz layer against a real database, not yet at the HTTP boundary (no routes exist to attack yet).
AI provider is mock-only; no live provider is connected (by design, Phase 3 scope per Master Spec §61).
Intent resolution and impact analysis are deterministic/keyword-based, not real language understanding.
assessFeasibility takes explicit capability keys, not raw text — the raw-text-to-capability-key mapping is P1-06's Requirements Engine job.
beginChangeFlow does not yet call assessFeasibility — wiring Feasibility into the change flow happens once P1-06's Requirements Engine can produce real capability keys from an idea.
Product Knowledge graph only exercises REQUIREMENT/WORKFLOW node types so far; no generation system yet produces Screen/Action/DataModel nodes (Phase 2 concern).
No automated e2e (Playwright) coverage yet — nothing customer-facing exists to test end-to-end.
nextAction: Begin P1-06: Product Intelligence, Requirements Engine, Business Model Brief, monetization recommendations, editable unit-economics assumptions, and operational-complexity analysis, generated via the mock AI provider and grounded in the Supported Capability Registry (Master Spec §17, §19-21).
